dedupe_keys.name: qgis stormwater pipe upstream and downstream node assignment

description: This PyQGIS script prepares stormwater network topology for hydraulic modelling. It takes a pipe line layer and a pit point layer with an ID and elevation field, matches each pipe endpoint to a nearby pit and writes upstream and downstream node IDs according to the relative pit elevations. The README gives QGIS 3.x console steps and field names to replace, and shows an output table intended for InfoWorks ICM import. A modeller could use it to add node references before checking connectivity and running a drainage simulation. The repository contains code and documentation, not a stormwater network dataset. Its nearest-pit and higher-elevation assumptions may fail at ambiguous crossings, pumped links, level pipes or inaccurate pit elevations; the result requires an engineering review before use. The script was not run and no output accuracy was measured here. GitHub metadata states MIT, with a licence file in the public tree. The method is geographically generic. Related resources are the user’s own pipe, pit and elevation layers, whose rights and quality stay separate. The main caveat is that elevation and endpoint proximity alone do not prove the intended hydraulic flow direction.
